fixes.explanation: Not a hint of that in verse 1. The Bible calls Job "…blameless and upright…" It also says he feared God and shunned evil, friend. Proud and stubborn would make a very different story.
The writer never calls Job clever or cunning. Verse 1 says he was "…blameless and upright, fearing God and shunning evil." That's about his character, not about being sneaky or sharp.

Yes, friend. Verse 3 says, "Job was the greatest man of all the people of the East." It comes right after the list of his flocks, herds and servants. That list of animals alone would fill a whole lot of cookie boxes.

The text says the opposite. Job 1:3 says, "Job was the greatest man of all the people of the East." The verse just finished counting his sheep, camels, oxen, donkeys and servants, and then it gives him that title.

He sends for his children to purify them. Then he rises early in the morning to offer burnt offerings for all of them. The text says this was Job's regular practice. I can barely get up early for a fresh batch.

The text gives us Job's own thought: "Perhaps my children have sinned and cursed God in their hearts." That's why he offers burnt offerings for all of them. I think that tells us how seriously Job takes his children's hearts.

No priest shows up in this passage. The reason the Bible gives is Job's own thought: "Perhaps my children have sinned and cursed God in their hearts." He's the one rising early in the morning to offer them.
Praise isn't the word. Satan says that if everything Job has is struck, "…he will surely curse You to Your face." He's betting on a curse.
The messenger says the Sabeans swooped down and took the oxen and donkeys away. It happens while the animals are plowing and grazing nearby. That's a rough way to start the news.
It's true, friend. Verse 16 says, "While he was still speaking, another messenger came and reported…" The first messenger is still speaking when the next one arrives. The news keeps coming.

No wild animals in this report. The second messenger says, "The fire of God fell from heaven. It burned and consumed the sheep and the servants…" Then he adds, "…and I alone have escaped to tell you!"
Goats aren't on Job's list, friend. Verse 3 names sheep, camels, oxen and donkeys. The Chaldeans formed three bands and raided the camels.
The text never says Job leaves the land of Uz. It says he stood up, tore his robe and shaved his head. Then "He fell to the ground and worshiped…"

Job says, "Blessed be the name of the LORD." It comes right after, "The LORD gave, and the LORD has taken away." He has just heard four messengers bring report after report of loss, and that's what he says. It's quiet and it's real.

Right, friend. Job 1:22 says, "In all this, Job did not sin or charge God with wrongdoing." He has lost his sheep, his camels and his children, and the text still says that. Satan said Job would curse God, and he didn't.
